claims.text: HRTEM can elucidate microstructural mechanisms associated with oxidation in the Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA.
EDS can elucidate elemental redistribution of nanoprecipitates during oxidation in the Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA.
The Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA is produced by additive manufacturing.
The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA contains dual nanoprecipitation.
High-temperature oxidation induces elemental redistribution and microstructural evolution involving the nanoprecipitates.
Observing microstructural evolution and elemental redistribution by HRTEM and EDS would improve understanding of the alloy's oxidation behavior.
Cast and wrought manufacturing routes constitute the baseline for comparison with the additively manufactured alloy.
Oxidation degradation limits the alloy's use at high temperatures.
The exact oxidation-degradation and nanoprecipitate-redistribution mechanisms are not fully understood.
In situ HRTEM and EDS during oxidation can measure microstructural evolution, elemental redistribution, and oxidation behavior.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis concerns whether HRTEM and EDS can elucidate oxidation mechanisms, whereas the falsification rule treats an absence of significant microstructural or compositional change as evidence that the methods cannot do so. A null observation could instead be a valid finding that no such redistribution occurs, so it does not decisively falsify the stated methodological hypothesis.
